# @suifengshiqu/skill-center
**English** · 简体中文
**Skill Center** adds one page to the DSH Web client where you can see every skill DSH can load from
your own directories, read one, switch it on or off, create one, install one from a link, and delet
e one into a trash you can restore from.
It is a third-party DSH plugin, not an official DeepSeek product. Licensed under the MIT License.
## Screenshots
| **The list** — every skill DSH can load, with its switch, its provenance and its problems. The row
above it is where a link goes. | **Creating one** — name, description and body, written into whiche
ver destination is selected. |
| **The trash** — what was deleted, where it came from, and one button to put it back. | **Deleting*
* — the confirmation says plainly that the skill goes to the trash, because a reversible delete is a
different promise from an erase. |

The screenshots are rendered from the shipped browser bundle over the Host's own
`Modal` stylesheet,

so the layout, colours and scrollbar are the ones the application
produces; only the surrounding ap

plication window is left out. `scripts/dev/render-shots.mjs`
regenerates them, in either theme.
## Where it appears
Two entry points, both opening the same page over one shared store:
- **Settings → Skill Center** — the settings section, so it sits with the rest of the configuration.
- **A `Skills` button in the composer**, in the input row beside the permission chip. It opens the
page in a modal, which is the quick path for switching a skill on or off mid-task.
The composer button lives in `conversation.input.left`. That is the only composer seat a plugin may
extend: the permission chip (`conversation.input.permission`) and the model picker (`conversation.in
put.model`) are `single` seats their own plugins already hold, so nothing can be inserted between th
em. The button also cannot deep-link to its settings section — `openSection` is internal to the sett
ings shell — so it opens the page directly instead.
Both entries follow the Host's theme:
## What it does
- **Lists** the skills under `$DSH_HOME/skills` (default `~/.dsh/skills`), any directory the profile

adds through `customSkillDirs`, and the current project's `<project>/.dsh/skills`.
- **Shows detail

s** for one skill: description, path, frontmatter block and instruction body.
- **Searches** by name

or description, and can hide the switched-off skills.
- **Switches a skill on or off** without losi

ng it: everything else about the file, including your own frontmatter keys, is left alone.
- **Creat

es a skill** from a name, a description and a body.
- **Installs a skill from a link** — a GitHub re

pository, a `/tree/` path inside one, a `.zip`, or a single `SKILL.md`.
- **Deletes a skill into a t

rash**, and restores it from there.
- **Writes new skills where you choose** — the destination contr

ol offers every directory the profile makes available, and the host accepts nothing else.
- **Report
s problems** the host would silently skip, such as a missing `description` or a name that is not keb

ab-case.
- Follows the Host's light or dark theme.
### Where new skills are written

The destinations come from the Host, not from the panel: `GET /roots` answers with the
profile's con

figured `customSkillDirs` followed by the default `$DSH_HOME/skills`. The
browser offers exactly tha

t list, and `POST /create` and `POST /install` refuse a
directory outside it — so "choose where to w

rite" does not become "write anywhere". With
one destination the control is a sentence; with several

, each is a button, because the
path is the point.
### Where deletion is allowed to reach
Removing something the user wrote is the one destructive thing here, so it is bounded:
- **Only DSH's own skills.** The trash covers the global roots (the DSH home and any `customSkillDir
s`). A project root — `<project>/.dsh/skills`, which is under version control — is never touched: Sk

ill Center may switch such a skill on or off, but it will not move it out of a repository.
- **Only
skills DSH can actually load.** A skill with broken frontmatter may have been misread, which is a re

ason to leave it alone rather than to move it.
- **Never through a link.** A symbolic link, or a Win
dows junction (which `lstat` reports as an ordinary directory), is refused by comparing the resolved

path with the requested one.
- **Never a plain erase.** The bundle is moved into `~/.dsh/skill-cent
er/trash` with a record of where it came from, and the panel can put it back byte-for-byte. Emptying

the trash is a separate, confirmed action.
[该节后续省略]
### What installing a link will and will not do
The download is treated as hostile input: entry paths may not escape the target, a bundle must have
a `SKILL.md` with a name DSH accepts and a description DSH requires, an existing name is refused rat
her than overwritten, and nothing is written until every one of those checks has passed. Private arc
hives and Zip64 are refused. Links to this machine (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `.local`) are not fetc
hed, and a single download is capped at 8 MB and 800 entries.
## What it does not do

- No other agents' directories (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, …).
- No Git repositories, no skill mark

etplace, no automatic updates.
- No creating or importing skills.
- No Trash.
- Nothing outside the
two roots above is ever read or written.
## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness with the Web client (tested against `0.2.0-rc.2`).
- Node.js `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.

eepSeek Harness with the Web client (tested against `0.2.0-rc.2`).
- Node.js `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0`.
### Why the build does not use a bundler
The development sandbox refuses `spawn` with piped stdio, which is how esbuild's JavaScript API star
ts its native service. The build therefore uses the TypeScript compiler in process, transpiling each
module to CommonJS and emitting:
- `lib/index.js` — one CommonJS file for the host, with `lib/package.json` marking the folder so the

package's own `"type": "module"` does not make Node parse it as ESM;
- `lib/client.js` — one lazy f
actory in the Web client's module-system format, with an internal module table and Host-shared libra
ries resolved through the shell's import map.
